notes.3: A number of candidates opted for D here, despite this distractor including the phrase ‘at constant speed’. These candidates probably did not realise that a car that is slowing down is accelerating, albeit negatively, so rejected option A, which was the key.
notes.6: This question on resultant force and acceleration was generally well answered, although distractor C was chosen quite commonly. These candidates failed to add the two resistive forces and then realise that their total was less than the force from the engine.
notes.11: The most common error here was caused by a lack of understanding that the useful work done by the escalator and the lift was the same in each case.
notes.12: This question concerned the simple barometer, and candidates needed to be aware that the difference in liquid levels could be used to find the atmospheric pressure. A significant number opted for C, failing to appreciate that the lower level was not zero.
notes.20: Many candidates were not aware that television pictures are transmitted from satellites to Earth using microwaves. The syllabus gives this as one of several specific examples of uses of electromagnetic waves.
notes.25: This question concerned the magnetisation of iron rods inside a solenoid. The most common mistake was to think that reversing the battery connections would cause the rods to repel, whereas before the change they had attracted.
notes.26: In any question involving echoes students must always take care that they have considered the time taken for the sound to travel out and return to its source, and many failed to do so here.
notes.29: A significant number of candidates chose D in this question, not realising that a thin wire would have a higher resistance than an otherwise similar thick wire.
notes.34: All distractors were popular in this question on fuses, with option C attracting more candidates than the key
notes.34d: . It was explained that the lamp was not faulty, so the wrong choice of fuse would not be apparent and the lamp would work normally. The point is that a fuse that is rated too highly for a particular purpose is a hidden danger.
